title: Bounded nondeterministic bit writer
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $j$ be one of the $k$ work tapes, let $Q$ be a controller state type, let $q_0\in Q$, let $\delta:Q\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to Q$, let $\mathrm{stop}:Q\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $\mathrm{bounded}$ be a Boolean flag. The resulting nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols starts in $\mathrm{run}(q_0)$. In state $\mathrm{done}$ it stays there with no writes or output and stationary heads; in state $\mathrm{run}(q)$ it enters $\mathrm{done}$ under the same idle action if $\mathrm{stop}(q)$ holds or if bounded mode is enabled and tape $j$ is blank at its head. Otherwise, for choice bit $b$, it writes $b$ on tape $j$, moves that tape's head right, leaves all other heads stationary without writing, emits no output, and enters $\mathrm{run}(\delta(q,b))$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A selected tape $j$ among the $k$ tapes
A state update function depending on a Boolean choice
A stopping predicate on controller states
